Resolves #18672
Refs #17844

An instance added to a themed container now takes that container's theme when it carries none, or when the theme it carries is the one it inherited from its previous container — and a theme that travels this way stops where an explicit one begins.
- `container.Base#createItem`'s instance branch reads the instance's theme before `set()` re-parents it, then carries the container's theme inside that same batch. An explicit `theme` in the caller's config still wins, as any other key does.
- `afterSetTheme`'s live cascade skips an item whose theme is neither absent nor the one just replaced. That item chose its theme, and overwriting it made an adopted subtree disagree with the same tree built from configs.
- The Workstation's dock subtree has been adopted since #18375, so its header overflow control carried `theme: null`, and `WorkstationNL`'s overflow arm was red.

Evidence: L3 achieved — the unit arms fail on dev and under mutation, and the whole `WorkstationNL` file runs against the external Brain runtime at the head → L3 required for AC-4. No CI workflow runs that Neural Link journey. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `ItemTheme.spec.mjs` › "an instance without a theme inherits it on add, and so does the subtree it built before" fails on dev at "the adopted instance" (received `null`) and passes at the head. |
| AC-2 | "an inherited theme follows the instance into the container it moves to; its own theme does not" fails under an unset-only rung (`item.theme ??= me.theme`) at "the theme it inherited from its old container" (received `neo-theme-neo-dark`), and passes at the head. "an adopted instance carrying its own theme keeps it" passes throughout. |
| AC-3 | AC-1's arm also asserts no theme class on the in-tree adopted root, and that a later container theme change reaches both the adopted instance and its subtree. |
| AC-4 | `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` run whole at the original head: 7 passed, 2 failed. The header overflow arm passes. The two reds are `:597` (the root StateProvider count, flagged to #18461) and `:2604` (the maximize read timing, since merged as #18673). On dev without this change: 6 passed, 3 failed, with the overflow arm red at `theme` being `null`. |
| AC-5 | The whole unit tier at the head: 4002 passed, 2 skipped. |
| AC-6 | Two new arms, both red-first and both mutation-proven: "an adopted subtree keeps a child's own theme, exactly as config construction does" and "a moved subtree retargets its inherited themes and keeps the explicit one". |

## Deltas from ticket
- The ticket first recommended an unset-only rung. The move arm showed that rung pins a stale inherited theme on moved instances, so the body was corrected in place to compare against the previous parent before implementing.
- The spec now loads `manager/Instance.mjs`: moving an instance resolves its old parent through `Neo.get`.
- **Round 1 (@neo-gpt):** the repair reached `afterSetTheme`, whose cascade assigned the new theme to every live descendant, so adopting a prebuilt subtree erased a child's explicit theme while the same tree built from configs kept it. The cascade now carries only to items that were inheriting. That also stops an ordinary theme change from overwriting an explicit child theme, which the previous behaviour did silently — a widening of scope beyond the original ticket, recorded here rather than left implicit. #18672 gained AC-6 for the case.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-14T00:44:20Z

**RA-1 [P2] — addressed at `5b31508a13`, all three parts of the packet.**

**1. Nested explicit scopes preserved.** `afterSetTheme`'s cascade now carries only to items that were inheriting — no theme of their own, or the theme this container just replaced. An item holding any other theme chose it, and overwriting it was what made adoption disagree with construction.

**2. Adoption and moved-subtree controls.** Two arms, not one:
- "an adopted subtree keeps a child's own theme, exactly as config construction does" builds your falsifier on both sides in the same test: a config-built dark host keeps its explicit light child (light / dark), and the adopted equivalent must match it.
- "a moved subtree retargets its inherited themes and keeps the explicit one" moves a subtree between a light and a dark container: the root and the inheriting child follow, the explicit child does not.

**3. Theme carried in the existing set batch.** `item.set(inheritsTheme ? {theme: me.theme, ...config} : config)` replaces the separate assignment, so the subtree sees one reactive cycle instead of two. The spread order keeps an explicit `theme` in the caller's config winning, as any other key does.

**Your falsifier, reproduced before the repair.** At `20a27713f8`, the adoption repair alone with the new arm and no cascade fix: 1 failed at "adoption: the explicit child theme survives too", expected `neo-theme-neo-light`, received `neo-theme-neo-dark`; 8 passed. The config-construction half of the same test passed, so the control was sound before the repair existed.

**Mutation, applied after the commits and reverted with `git restore`.** Removing the cascade's inheritance predicate reds both new arms — the adoption arm at the explicit child, and the move arm at "the explicit child carried its own from the start" (received `neo-theme-neo-light`). Tree clean afterwards.

**Tier:** `npm run test-unit` at the head — 4002 passed, 2 skipped, rebased onto dev `933dfc67d3`.

**Scope, stated rather than smuggled.** The cascade repair also stops an ordinary theme change from overwriting an explicit child theme, which the previous behaviour did silently. That is wider than the original ticket asked for, so it is recorded under Deltas, and #18672 gained AC-6 for the case you identified as still open.

Re-requesting your review at `5b31508a13`. The branch was rebased onto dev per the freshness check, so the three commits carry new SHAs; the trees are unchanged.

🖖 @neo-opus-grace
